column5: The source already gives level-three Brown and level-four Rokhlin formulas. Another special value is an instance; a general intrinsic interpretation needs a bridge beyond these formulas.

Quantum 6j asymptotics are only suggested as a route; cancellation and passage from tetrahedra to manifold growth remain. Defining an artificial sequence from volume would evade the quantum-invariant context.
The SL(2,C) Chern-Simons explanation must be generalized to other noncompact groups with a well-defined invariant and asymptotic statement. No cheap construction supplies these bridges.
A decorated cobordism functor containing QHI needs phase, gluing and connected-sum compatibility, not merely a multiplicative number on closed manifolds.

The source itself proposes KN=JN^N but says fixed R-matrix parameters do not satisfy the needed global decoration argument. Evaluating one link cannot determine the relation as functions of all links.

All modular categories are requested; constructing a pointed category or listing small ranks would supply only source-known families. The appended series belongs to the following question and is not a reduction.
Both spin and spin-c HQFT extensions and their 1+1 algebra structures are requested. Ordinary crossed pi-algebras in the source do not discharge spin gluing or both classifications.

The geometric vector space is already known; the missing object is the vector associated geometrically to every bounding 3-manifold with gluing compatibility. Transport through an abstract vector-space isomorphism misses the geometric demand.
The source reports finite genus-one images and infinite higher-genus examples. A general given-TQFT finiteness criterion is needed; repeating either family is no full solution.
All three classification tasks include arbitrary finite simple-object sets, fusion symbols and finite-depth subfactors. Known ADE or finite-group examples cannot qualify.
Ocneanu finiteness is reported internally, but does not decide existence or recover all presentations for an arbitrary given TQFT. No effective recognition mechanism was found.

The source already discusses alpha-induction and answers under modularity. The noninvertible S-matrix case requires a comparison of TQFTs compatible with restricted 6j symbols; modular specialization is insufficient.

The preceding paragraph already reports a Longo-Rehren RT-type realization. The question asks for the degenerate-braiding description/minimal extension; repeating that paragraph or the nondegenerate tensor-square case earns no credit.

Configuration integrals already exist. Localization must control hidden/anomaly strata uniformly for each finite-type invariant; a Casson-only formula is a restricted case of the all-invariants request.

Naively reducing rational diagram coefficients modulo p does not handle denominators divisible by p or the universal all-degree construction. No integral bridge or characteristic-p replacement was established.

The source already extends Kontsevich to KTG and states finite presentation by operations. A new existence proof must construct compatible initial data and prove all relations, not cite the existing extension.
The source suggests LMO and its even part only for rational homology spheres. Both universal invariants for closed 3-manifolds in KTG algebra require more than this restricted candidate.

The primary list cites existing computer-discovered biquandle decorations. A new presentation needs mixed virtual/classical Reidemeister relations and nontrivial virtual structure; no new verified mechanism was found.
The task includes definitions/classification, a flyping theorem and unstabilized surface weaves. A single diagram or planar Tait adaptation leaves major requested bridges unproved.

The request is for new geometric/topological interpretations of both Jones and Khovanov theories. Repeating bracket state sums or already known categorification does not meet novelty; no full new interpretation was supplied.

A constant set map is vacuous and loses the source's structure-enlarging requirement. Turaev's descending construction uses flat crossing data absent for free knots; invariance under the added identifications needs a new bridge.

Parity must be extracted from the specified cobordism and remain compatible with its internal moves. Constant even parity would be a routine degenerate substitution; a nontrivial intrinsic construction was not established.

An arbitrary set-theoretic retraction would bypass diagrammatic functorial projection. Circle-graph realizability is not visibly preserved by an ad hoc vertex deletion under all graph Reidemeister moves.

Bouchet obstructions are graph-realizability data, but a vertex parity must obey all move axioms, including the cyclically six-edge-connected objective. A Boolean graph-wide obstruction is not such a parity.

Frobenius extension and Rasmussen generalizations require chain maps, invariance and filtration behavior for rigid orientable graph-links. Reusing the ordinary link complex does not supply the graph-move bridge.

Ambient graph-link equivalence must be replaced by an equivalence through realizable diagrams. Non-realizable individual graphs already discussed in Section 7 do not refute this restricted-move equivalence claim.

The missing MathDB citation is restored to reference184 Subsection8.9 in the source. A group must be analogous to that construction and invariant under graph moves; assigning a trivial group is not substantive.

The collection gives finite-covolume Kleinian Gamma but does not spell out the comparison class in this question. Products with finite-quotient-invisible groups would exploit this omission, not solve intended profinite rigidity. No admissible full-class counterexample was found.

The intended finitely generated residually finite comparison cannot be replaced by arbitrary groups with invisible factors. Morales supplies two-generator subgroup restrictions and hierarchy-class rigidity, not an unrestricted classification.
The comparison classes are explicitly Kleinian groups or compact 3-manifold groups. Unrestricted group products do not apply, and a pair in another geometric category would miss the hypotheses.
Need to detect knot-complement status among hyperbolic torus-boundary manifolds from the profinite completion. First-homology matching is necessary information but not a recognition certificate.
Enumerating reducing curves semidecides a yes case but gives no terminating no case. A full algorithm requires an effective obstruction or a complete finite search bound for the given splitting.

The body gives finite generation for g>=3, infinite generation for genus2 and an H3 obstruction for genus3. These known cases do not determine all Fk and homology finiteness as functions of genus and degree.

The source defines lengths of shortest homology cycles and notes L is nonsmooth and nonproper in higher genus. Genus-one critical-point computation is already an exercise; no higher-genus Morse replacement or critical-set classification was obtained.

The target asks for a (6g-8)-obstructor and a proper expanding map into thick Teichmuller space. Choosing a join with correct formal obstructor dimension alone does not build the required map; statement includes an unrelated footnote tail.
The source fixes word-geodesic quasiconvexity and distinguishes it from Teichmuller convex cocompactness. Linear distortion alone is insufficient; a full subgroup criterion is not furnished.

Group entropy is the infimum over finite generating sets, not pseudo-Anosov dilatation. The source already proves positivity through linear quotients; explicit genus and Johnson-depth asymptotics need uniform sharp controls beyond this.
All subgroups L in wedge3H/H and all g>=3 are quantified. The source gives endpoint information but interpolation requires structural finiteness criteria, not another endpoint instance.

Yildiz2002.09151v1 Theorem1 and proof give three involutions for all g>=6, covering the highlighted g>=7 clause; Korkmaz1904.08156v2 gives g>=8 and four for g>=3. Full low-genus sharp classification is not certified here. No credit for rederiving these constructions.

The body defines ordered distinct dilatation-spectrum density separately from counting mapping classes. Random-walk genericity or one subgroup example cannot replace densities for level and Johnson subgroups in this ordering.

The body already proves 2(g-2+n)<=dimCW<=(7g-8)/2 rounded down plus2n by stratified Morse theory. Reprinting these bounds or small-genus contractibility is not new; improving them needs divisor-fiber analysis.

Topology at infinity is linked to compact-type Torelli low homology by duality. Known genus-two behavior and the boundary sphere of J3 do not compute T3 compact-type ends; no cheap end calculation survives this distinction.

The full graded cohomology at infinity of T3 compact type is requested. The Gysin suggestion needs the reducible-divisor complex and attaching data; knowing dimensions or a single low degree is insufficient.

N is nonorientable with punctures and Mod(N) includes all diffeomorphisms. Importing orientable rigidity or a stable-genus theorem would omit low-complexity cases and source domain; no full automorphism classification checked.

The source already states residual finiteness of Mg. A nontrivial Torelli separating twist can therefore be detected by some finite quotient, which cannot factor through Sp. This is a routine existential deduction; explicit accessible representations and source's intended new tools remain the substantive issue.

A finite-dimensional faithful candidate for general higher-genus Mg or boundary variant is wanted. The regular permutation representation is infinite-dimensional, and known braid/genus-two linearity is explicitly listed as outside the dream problem.

The compact U(1) torus Fourier-orbit decomposition and covering interpretation are already given. Nonabelian groups lack this linear character basis; no decomposition/geometry bridge for the irreducible constituents was obtained.

The body distinguishes dense image of rho from dense mapping-class orbit and reports genus-zero counterexamples to the naive criterion. Reusing those counterexamples is source-known; general necessary and sufficient conditions remain unsupported.

Brown's KAM examples are for relative one-holed-torus varieties; the source explicitly suggests branched covers. A lift must prove pseudo-Anosov behavior and a positive-measure nonergodic region on the entire closed-surface character variety, not only on a lower-dimensional fixed locus.

The source already exhibits a 6g-6-dimensional thickening via the Euler-class component and obstructions to actions on the surface. A minimum dimension needs matching bounds; reproducing this upper bound is a source-known instance.
